on_the_settled_value.why_this_is_the_right_statistic: the settled value is not an average of a drifting joint -- every one of the 12 settled windows in BOTH runs holds a single value across all ten of its 10 Hz samples, and each sits on an exact encoder count. Run 1 and run 2 landed on the SAME two counts: out-stroke count 538 (-47.285 deg) and in-stroke count 530 (-46.582 deg). This is not two averages that happened to agree; it is the same discrete count twice.

on_the_6_cycle_mean.note: the whole 0.029 deg is run 1's single first-cycle 2-count event

family_context.reading: the plan asks this run's spread to be set against L1's demonstrated 0.230 deg. L3's is 0.000 deg on the settled value and 0.029 deg on the 6-cycle mean -- an order of magnitude smaller. Two further facts stop L1's 0.230 from being treated as a family-wide bound that L3 must inherit. First, L1's large BETWEEN-run spread comes with a large WITHIN-run scatter (per-run sd 0.123, 0.149, 0.065; its cycles bounce between 2 and 8 counts inside a single run) and L3 has none of that -- run 2's within-run sd is exactly 0.000. Second, L2 has MORE runs than L1 (4 vs 3) and a between-run spread of only 0.072 deg, so 0.230 is the family's outlier, not its norm. The honest limit is that n=2 runs cannot prove L3's population spread is truly zero; it can only show that the two runs landed on the same encoder count.

required_conclusion.question: is L3 separable from the L5/L0 bracket?
required_conclusion.answer: NO -- and with a two-run number precise enough to say so, L3 now reads as the LOWEST MEMBER of that bracket rather than a third intermediate value.
required_conclusion.arithmetic: L3 sits 1.468 counts from L5. L5 and L0 -- the two legs already accepted as ONE bracket -- sit 1.536 counts apart. L3's distance to the bracket is therefore SMALLER than the bracket's own internal spacing. Accepting {L5, L0} as one group forces {L3, L5, L0} to be one group at the same standard. The real discontinuity in the five-leg series is L2->L3 at 3.041 counts, more than double any other adjacent gap.

two_questions_kept_apart.q: is L3's VALUE distinguishable from L5's value?
two_questions_kept_apart.a: Yes. 1.468 counts against a measured between-run spread of 0.000-0.334 counts. L3 and L5 are different numbers and a gait should not use one for the other.

two_questions_kept_apart.q: is L3 SEPARABLE FROM the L5/L0 bracket as a cluster?
two_questions_kept_apart.a: No, for the spacing reason above. These answer different things and both are reported because conflating them is how a single number turns into a wrong bracket.

required_conclusion.what_run1_could_not_say: run 1's gap to L5 was 0.158 deg against an assumed-applicable 0.230 deg spread, so it could not tell 'L3 is a third value' from 'L3 belongs to the high bracket and read low'. The replicate resolves it: L3's own spread is 0.000, the gap is a real 1.47 counts, and the spacing test places L3 inside the bracket. This REVERSES run 1's tentative 'not a two-bracket picture' reading.
required_conclusion.gait_consequence: the open question that justified this run was whether L3's number could be used as a per-leg gait constant. It now can: L3 = 8.0 encoder counts (-0.703 deg), reproduced exactly across two independent runs. That is the deliverable.

plan_question_2_drift.detail: all six cycles identical at -0.703; the post-hoc monotonicity check reports no growth.

plan_question_1_loaded_vs_unloaded.detail: out-stroke error -0.152 and in-stroke +0.551 on every one of the six cycles, matching run 1's cycles 2-6 exactly. Peak current on the moving joint 0.026 A against a 0.75 A trip -- the same 0.026 A run 1 measured. Loaded stroke draws roughly 4-8x the unloaded stroke (0.0088-0.0116 A vs 0.0012-0.0030 A) at loads of 4.0-5.1 % vs 3.2-3.9 %.
